copy.title: Network & sponsor pitch
copy.body: First Failure is a weekly podcast in which a well-known founder tells the full story of the startup that failed before the one that worked. Its touchstones are How I Built This with Guy Raz, This Week in Startups, Acquired and The Tim Ferriss Show. Qloo affinity puts Masters of Scale at fit 0.99 and My First Million at 0.98, both Mid-list (Top 2% and Top 3%). Noah Kagan Presents is at 0.96 and All-In with Chamath, Jason, Sacks & Friedberg at 0.95. The category has room at the top: Entrepreneurs on Fire (Top 0.28%) and StartUp Podcast (Top 0.41%) both reach Breakout size. StartUp Podcast is the closest in spirit, since it is built on the story of a company. The audience skews male and 45–54, and leans toward business, technology and entrepreneurship. For sponsors, that means a base of founders and operators. Qloo's emerging markets include San Jose, San Francisco, Miami, Boise, Fresno and Phoenix. This is aggregate taste, not a forecast.
copy.hint: Comps and audience for a network, guest or sponsor pitch.
copy.author: llm

copy.title: Who it's for
copy.body: The audience over-indexes male (0.51) and 45–54 (+0.42). It under-indexes 55+ (-0.44) and 35–44 (-0.31), with 30–34 roughly level (+0.01). Its taste descriptors are business, technology, entrepreneurship and philosophy, with documentary, science fiction and true crime alongside. The same audience also likes Acquired-style deep dives, plus How to Lead: Wisdom from the World's Greatest CEOs, Founders, and Game Changers, The Social Dilemma and AlphaGo. They follow Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz and Scott Galloway. Emerging markets include San Jose, San Francisco, Miami, Boise, Fresno and Phoenix.

• Fans of My First Million: one founder, one failed idea, the full account and what came next.

kit.headline: How I Built This with Guy Raz, This Week in Startups, Acquired and The Tim Ferriss Show listeners already sit in the same lane, and Masters of Scale and My First Million show it is a deep one; the open slot is the failure that came before the success.
kit.summary: First Failure sits in the entrepreneurship interview lane, with Masters of Scale and Noah Kagan Presents as the closest fits. It is built for a male-leaning audience that skews 45–54, and the touchstones are business, technology and philosophy. Lead with the premise: one founder, one full failure story, each week. Use the Breakout-size comps Entrepreneurs on Fire and StartUp Podcast to show the ceiling for the format.
